requirements.requirement: Establish a usable integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was configured with a rule covering /etc, initialized a root-only database containing 2,389 /etc records, and produced a clean final check. The package, configuration, database, and database hash also persisted across the restart.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A controlled file addition was reported by exact path with a non-clean AIDE result. The probe was removed, and the daily checker then generated a root-only clean report while crond was active and enabled.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered configuration/database/scheduler state, and a final clean integrity report.
limitations: The daily script was executed manually; an actual time-triggered cron invocation was not captured, although crond was directly shown active and enabled.
Package-manager health snapshots timed out both before and after execution, so overall RPM consistency was not independently observed.
The lifecycle inventory does not cover /var/tmp or specifically verify cleanup or retention of auxiliary installer/reboot logs and the configuration backup.

operational_hygiene.summary: No clearly unnecessary mutation was established. Installing AIDE, replacing its configuration, initializing the database, adding the daily checker, and adjusting volatile metadata coverage all directly supported the task. The controlled probe was bounded and removed (cmd-74385f19d94b4669, cmd-8587091fdc864a1f). Terminating the stale yum check enabled the required package installation (cmd-b736793db87e4424). The failed initial configuration attempt created a rollback copy before aborting, a reasonable safety measure rather than an unrelated experiment (cmd-a7dd38ce22634a82). After execution there were no failed services or unexpected listening sockets.
